cpi_release_2026_10.bls_handling: BLS notice '12-Month Percent Changes, October 2026': because BLS did not collect October 2025 survey data (2025 lapse in appropriations), it cannot publish October 2026 12-month percent changes for indexes where the October 2025 index is unavailable, which includes all items and all items less food and energy. A few narrower series that do have an October 2025 index still show a 12-month change (e.g. gasoline NSA, reported +37.4%). BLS said the missing October 2025 data cannot be obtained retroactively (spokesperson Cody Parkinson). For the October 2025 index gap BLS had carried forward bi-monthly August 2025 prices for other series; no official 11-month or synthetic substitute YoY was published. Last published annual rates remain September 2026: headline 3.7%, core 2.6% (secondary).
cpi_release_2026_10.consequence_for_tool: No official value exists for cpi_yoy_override / core_cpi_yoy_override['2026-10'], so both stay empty. Never put a computed or interpolated YoY there. The tool therefore drops core_cpi_yoy and inflation_direction for the 2026-10 CPI (reweighted, -5 required_submetric_missing_but_reweightable) and uses PCE only for the headline shock. The November 2026 CPI (2026-12-10) has a 2025-11 base and is computable; the 2027-01 CPI run's t-3 core YoY (2026-10) stays permanently missing.

cpi_release_2026_10.bls_handling: BLS notice '12-Month Percent Changes, October 2026': because BLS did not collect October 2025 survey data (2025 lapse in appropriations), it cannot publish October 2026 12-month percent changes for indexes where the October 2025 index is unavailable, which includes all items and all items less food and energy. A few narrower series that do have an October 2025 index still show a 12-month change (e.g. gasoline NSA, reported +37.4%). BLS said the missing October 2025 data cannot be obtained retroactively (spokesperson Cody Parkinson). For the October 2025 index gap BLS had carried forward bi-monthly August 2025 prices for other series; no official 11-month or synthetic substitute YoY was published. Last published annual rates remain September 2026: headline 3.7%, core 2.6% (secondary).
cpi_release_2026_10.consequence_for_tool: No official value exists for cpi_yoy_override / core_cpi_yoy_override['2026-10'], so both stay empty. Never put a computed or interpolated YoY there. The tool therefore drops core_cpi_yoy and inflation_direction for the 2026-10 CPI (reweighted, -5 required_submetric_missing_but_reweightable) and uses PCE only for the headline shock. The November 2026 CPI (2026-12-10) has a 2025-11 base and is computable; the 2027-01 CPI run's t-3 core YoY (2026-10) stays permanently missing.
